review: The picker hardcoded gpt-5.4-mini while the current shared policy accepts only its declared pinned IDs. The menu now derives entries from that exact policy list, keeping profile choices unchanged.
Pinned entries display their exact model ID and a neutral exact-model description. The stale lowest-cost claim is removed; no current provider availability or pricing claim is made.

The existing mounted shell test now selects each policy-listed model, verifies no turn starts on selection, checks the submitted explicit contract and persisted value, and remounts to verify the selected choice remains visible without another turn.

Before the production edit, the mounted regression could not find the current policy-listed choice. An earlier invocation before editing the fixture selected zero tests; that receipt is retained and not used as regression evidence.
Both selected files matched the public preview before this slice. Runtime sampling, provider funding and shared model policy are unchanged.

Adding the existing shell suite to compiler roots exposed ten invalid UUID mock values and three void-callback return mismatches. Deterministic valid UUIDs now replace those fixture identities consistently, including trace assertions; callbacks retain their pushes and return void. Original behavior assertions are preserved. Intermediate tests and compiler output are retained.
limits: Unfrozen unpublished source qualification, not installed or real-model availability evidence.
Mounted tests inject a fake turn transport. The existing shared policy is the application contract, not evidence that an external provider accepts a model.
